title: Paeoniae Radix Alba-Chuanxiong Rhizoma herbal pair alleviates trigeminal nucleus caudalis neuroinflammation in chronic migraine associated with P2Y12R/PPARgamma-related NF-kappaB signaling.
authors: Liu, Lirong; Feng, Menghan; Liu, Jie; Cai, Shengnan; Cong, Shiyu; Xu, Yifan; Li, Yueting; Gao, Jiale; Xiao, Hongbin
one_liner_zh: 该文研究中药药对缓解慢性偏头痛神经炎症的机制，涉及P2Y12R/PPARgamma信号通路，虽用分子对接和MD模拟，但对象为蛋白-小分子互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Neuroinflammation in the trigeminal nucleus caudalis (TNC) plays an important role in the pathological process of chronic migraine (CM). The Paeoniae Radix Alba (Baishao, BS)-Chuanxiong Rhizoma (Chuanxiong, CX) herb pair (BSCX) is widely used in the treatment of migraine, but its mechanism of action and representative candidate constituents remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of BSCX on TNC neuroinflammation and to explore its representative candidate constituents and potential mechanisms associated with microglial inflammatory phenotype-related changes and P2Y12R/PPARgamma-related NF-kappaB signaling. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A nitroglycerin-induced rat model of CM was used to evaluate the anti-migraine effects of BSCX through behavioral testing and molecular analyses. ELISA, RT-qPCR, immunofluorescence staining, and Western blot were used to evaluate changes in inflammatory factors, pro-/anti-inflammatory phenotype-related markers, and pathway-related proteins in blood samples and the TNC. Potential candidate constituents in the TNC were identified using ultrahigh-performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole time-of-flight tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-QTOF-MS). The associations between the candidate constituents and their putative targets were further investigated by integrating molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS) assays, and cellular thermal shift assays (CETSA). A lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced BV2 cell model was established, with additional interventions using the P2Y12R agonist 2-MeS-ADP and the PPARgamma inhibitor GW9662. Flow cytometry was used to assess CD86/CD206-positive cells and phagocytic activity, while immunofluorescence staining and Western blot were used to evaluate related protein expression and signaling changes. RESULTS: BSCX alleviated NTG-induced migraine-like behaviors and pain sensitization. Compared with the model group, the medium- and high-dose BSCX groups showed reduced spontaneous head-scratching episodes, increased periorbital mechanical withdrawal threshold, and prolonged thermal withdrawal latency. BSCX reduced the expression of CGRP and c-Fos in the TNC by 16.2%-21.6% and 19.6%-55.1%, respectively. BSCX also reduced serum TNF-alpha and IL-1beta levels while increasing IL-10 and TGF-beta levels. Immunofluorescence analysis of the TNC further showed that BSCX decreased the proportion of iNOS(+)/Iba1(+) cells by 49.8%-86.2% and increased the proportion of Arg-1(+)/Iba1(+) cells by 222%-271%. These changes were accompanied by reduced expression of P2Y12R/RhoA/ROCK2/NF-kappaB-related proteins and increased PPARgamma expression. Among the constituents detected in the TNC, benzoylpaeoniflorin (Ben) and senkyunolide I (SENI) reduced LPS-induced TNF-alpha release by 13.7% and 21.6%, respectively, at 2.5 muM, and increased IL-10 release by 18.1% and 21.0%, respectively, at 5 muM. Molecular docking showed favorable binding energies for the P2Y12R-Ben and PPARgamma-SENI complexes. Molecular dynamics simulations further showed that their binding free energies were -23.31 and -22.06 kcal/mol, respectively, which were more favorable than those of the corresponding cross-combinations. In DARTS and CETSA assays, Ben enhanced the protease resistance and thermal stability of P2Y12R, while SENI enhanced the protease resistance and thermal stability of PPARgamma. In reversal experiments, 2-MeS-ADP increased the phagocytic activity and P2Y12R expression relative to the Ben group by 40.6% and 76.8%, respectively; GW9662 increased phagocytic activity by 41.7% and decreased PPARgamma expression by 26.8% relative to the SENI group. CONCLUSIONS: BSCX alleviates TNC neuroinflammation in CM, accompanied by regulation of pro-/anti-inflammatory phenotype-related markers and changes in P2Y12R/RhoA/ROCK2/NF-kappaB signaling and PPARgamma-related signaling. Ben and SENI may represent candidate constituents associated with the P2Y12R- and PPARgamma-related signaling branches, respectively, and may partly contribute to the pharmacological effects of the BSCX herb pair against CM.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：三叉神经尾核（TNC）中的神经炎症在慢性偏头痛（CM）的病理过程中发挥重要作用。白芍（Baishao, BS）-川芎（Chuanxiong, CX）药对（BSCX）广泛用于偏头痛的治疗，但其作用机制和代表性候选成分仍不清楚。研究目的：本研究旨在评估BSCX对TNC神经炎症的影响，并探讨其与微胶质细胞炎症表型相关变化及P2Y12R/PPARgamma相关NF-kappaB信号相关的代表性候选成分和潜在机制。材料与方法：采用硝酸甘油诱导的CM大鼠模型，通过行为测试和分子分析评估BSCX的抗偏头痛作用。使用ELISA、RT-qPCR、免疫荧光染色和Western blot评估血液样本和TNC中炎症因子、促/抗炎表型相关标志物及通路相关蛋白的变化。使用超高效液相色谱-四极杆飞行时间串联质谱（UHPLC-QTOF-MS）鉴定TNC中的潜在候选成分。通过整合分子对接、分子动力学模拟、药物亲和响应靶标稳定性（DARTS）分析和细胞热位移分析（CETSA），进一步研究候选成分与其推定靶标之间的关联。建立脂多糖（LPS）诱导的BV2细胞模型，并使用P2Y12R激动剂2-MeS-ADP和PPARgamma抑制剂GW9662进行额外干预。使用流式细胞术评估CD86/CD206阳性细胞和吞噬活性，同时使用免疫荧光染色和Western blot评估相关蛋白表达和信号变化。结果：BSCX减轻了NTG诱导的偏头痛样行为和疼痛敏化。与模型组相比，中剂量和高剂量BSCX组显示自发抓头次数减少、眶周机械 withdrawal 阈值增加和热 withdrawal 潜伏期延长。BSCX将TNC中CGRP和c-Fos的表达分别降低了16.2%-21.6%和19.6%-55.1%。BSCX还降低了血清TNF-alpha和IL-1beta水平，同时增加了IL-10和TGF-beta水平。TNC的免疫荧光分析进一步显示，BSCX将iNOS(+)/Iba1(+)细胞比例降低了49.8%-86.2%，并将Arg-1(+)/Iba1(+)细胞比例增加了222%-271%。这些变化伴随着P2Y12R/RhoA/ROCK2/NF-kappaB相关蛋白表达降低和PPARgamma表达增加。在TNC中检测到的成分中，苯甲酰芍药苷（Ben）和川芎内酯I（SENI）在2.5 μM浓度下分别将LPS诱导的TNF-alpha释放降低了13.7%和21.6%，并在5 μM浓度下将IL-10释放分别增加了18.1%和21.0%。分子对接显示P2Y12R-Ben和PPARgamma-SENI复合物具有有利的结合能。分子动力学模拟进一步显示，它们的结合自由能分别为-23.31和-22.06 kcal/mol，比相应的交叉组合更有利。在DARTS和CETSA分析中，Ben增强了P2Y12R的蛋白酶抗性和热稳定性，而SENI增强了PPARgamma的蛋白酶抗性和热稳定性。在逆转实验中，相对于Ben组，2-MeS-ADP将吞噬活性和P2Y12R表达分别增加了40.6%和76.8%；相对于SENI组，GW9662将吞噬活性增加了41.7%，并将PPARgamma表达降低了26.8%。结论：BSCX减轻了CM中的TNC神经炎症，伴随着促/抗炎表型相关标志物的调节以及P2Y12R/RhoA/ROCK2/NF-kappaB信号和PPARgamma相关信号的变化。Ben和SENI可能分别代表与P2Y12R和PPARgamma相关信号分支相关的候选成分，并可能部分贡献于BSCX药对对抗CM的药理效应。
